mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% and remains there for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the prior quarter predicts weak demand growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the GDP and housing decline co-occur with a strong labor market (UNRATE > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for three consecutive months signals improving supply capacity and corporate earnings momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration persists but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 100k signals a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and often precedes equity pullbacks; this predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% with no contemporaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS unchanged) signals a policy lag, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL MoM change > 0.33% AND FEDFUNDS MoM change == 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat predicts weakening consumer demand without supply constraint relief, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS MoM change < -1% AND INDPRO MoM change between -0.2% and 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.4 percentage points while payroll employment (PAYEMS) also declines signals a deteriorating labor market, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE MoM change < -0.4% AND PAYEMS MoM change < -50000
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A three-month consecutive rise in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 0.3% per month, without a corresponding rise in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL flat), signals improving supply capacity without inflationary pressure, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM change >= 0.3% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL MoM change between -0.1% and 0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes.
